method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase; not independent or human review.
scope: All twenty-two translated content blocks on non-enumerability and two forms of Cantor diagonalization.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A set is nonenumerable when no surjection from positive integers exhausts it; to prove this, construct an element omitted from every proposed one-way infinite list.
samples.checks: Surjectivity, positive-integer domain, omitted-element criterion and comparison language are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Given a list of infinite binary sequences, define the nth bit of a new sequence by flipping the nth bit of the nth listed sequence.
samples.checks: Array coordinates, case definition, equivalent subtraction formula and all bit values remain exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The constructed sequence differs from listed sequence k at coordinate k, contradicting the assumption that every binary sequence occurs on the list.
samples.checks: Identity-at-every-coordinate, n=k specialization, both binary cases and the final contradiction are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For any list Z1,Z2,… of subsets of positive integers, define Z-bar={n∈PosInt:n∉Zn}; it differs from Zk on membership of k for every k.
samples.checks: Power-set scope, set comprehension, biconditionals, arbitrariness of k and extensional difference are unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The power-set proof can be pictured as toggling diagonal membership in a set-membership array, and the exercises request the same method for Pow(Nat) and positive-integer-valued functions.
samples.checks: The four sample sets, diagonal include/exclude pattern, exercise domains and function-list conclusion remain exact.

limitations: T073 is provisional descriptive vocabulary open to correction.
No independent linguistic certification has been performed.
